diff_is_the_audit_trail.statement: No Slack decisions, no verbal approvals. If it's not in a merged PR in this repo, it's not policy.
diff_is_the_audit_trail.how_to_apply: Treat any standards claim that isn't backed by a merged PR here as non-authoritative, regardless of who said it or how confidently.

mechanical_proxies_not_vibes.statement: Where a rule needs a threshold (code needs restructuring, coverage is adequate), use a measurable mechanical proxy — duplication percentage, cyclomatic complexity — not a vibes-based judgment call. Deliberately reject proxies that don't hold up under scrutiny even though they're easy to compute: file-length is the canonical rejected example, because a long file can be one well-factored module and a short file can be a tangle.
mechanical_proxies_not_vibes.how_to_apply: When proposing a new gate, ask what it's a proxy for and whether a shorter/longer version of the same problem would slip past it.

real_usage_over_aspirational_claims.statement: A standard that claims enforced:true without a real CI step behind it is worse than no standard at all — it's a false attestation that erodes trust in every other enforced:true claim in the file. Standards content must describe what's actually true in consuming repos' CI today, not what the org intends to be true eventually. Aspirational controls belong under recommendation, not enforced.
real_usage_over_aspirational_claims.source: 2026-07-25 real-usage audit — found security.yaml asserting dependency_vulnerability_scanning enforced:true with zero audit step in either consumer repo's CI.
real_usage_over_aspirational_claims.how_to_apply: Before setting enforced:true on any new rule, confirm a CI step (or equivalent live mechanism) actually blocks on it in at least one consuming repo. If not, use recommendation: true and open the CI PR first.

yaml_is_source_of_truth.statement: Edit src/*.yaml. Never hand-edit standards/, profiles/, or coverage/*.json — they are generated by generate.ts and any manual edit is silently overwritten on the next generation run.
yaml_is_source_of_truth.how_to_apply: Applies to this plugin too — the MCP resources this plugin serves are read-only views of standards/*.json; nothing an agent does through this plugin should attempt to write standards content back.

standard_should_match_real_work_patterns.statement: A standard aimed at the wrong shape of work (e.g. curating for a web-API Python stack when the org's real Python is data-pipeline microservices) doesn't get ignored gracefully — it gets silently bypassed while looking authoritative. Aim standards at what a `find` across consuming repos actually shows, not at what the domain "usually" looks like industry-wide.
standard_should_match_real_work_patterns.source: 2026-07-25 real-usage audit — python.yaml was curated for fastapi/flask/sqlalchemy while the org's real Python usage (~2,181 files) is concentrated in insights-data-platform's data-ingestion pipelines using uv, pyarrow, and psycopg.
standard_should_match_real_work_patterns.how_to_apply: Before adding or re-scoping a domain, grep the actual consuming repos first — don't extrapolate from what the ecosystem typically looks like.
